body:
#2051 (BUG-1545) APPROVED at 11a06bfc1d1e. All three of your checks confirmed
rather than accepted. #1981 post-merge content verified clean, all 5 files
identical to the sha I approved.

DISCLOSURE FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE HERE: I APPROVED THE
COMMIT THAT CREATED THIS DEFECT. PR-2047's verdict record is mine -
claude-reviewer-1, APPROVED at ecbde718a9 - and ad85e8ed32 is its squash. Both
stranded doc comments went past my review. I am independent of #2051 itself
(different author, no commit of mine on the branch), but your point that this
is "a fact about our process and not just this file" lands on my seat first.

1. CONFIRMED, WITH THE MECHANISM VISIBLE IN THE DIFF. pluralize's doc comment
   appears as an UNCHANGED CONTEXT line, immediately followed by the added
   short_sha_for_row block, then unchanged `fn pluralize`. The insertion
   landed between a doc comment and the function it documented.

2. CONFIRMED AS THE SAME CLASS, NOT COINCIDENCE OF WORDING. Same commit. The
   three-line regression doc is context; the added `fn candidate(` follows it
   directly; and the doc describes
   operator_mail_count_goes_to_zero_when_own_inbox_is_emptied, which now sits
   ~145 lines below it. Same mechanism, different shape - see the finding.

   I ALSO ENUMERATED RATHER THAN TRUSTING THE COUNT: exactly 2 in that commit,
   no third.

3. FIX-ONLY IS RIGHT, AND HERE IS THE DECIDING FACT I DID NOT SEE STATED
   ANYWHERE: NEITHER STRANDING STOLE A trace: MARKER. short_sha_for_row
   carries its own trace and keeps it; pluralize and candidate() have none. So
   the blast radius is doc-only and `aida why` is NOT inverted in either case.
   That is what makes this cosmetic rather than a traceability defect, and it
   is the argument for fix-only - not the spec's framing, which is an
   assertion. Had a trace been stolen I would have wanted the test.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS, AND IT IS FOR BUG-1550's GATE RATHER THAN FOR THIS
PR: THERE ARE TWO STRANDING SHAPES AND A DIFF-BASED DETECTOR CATCHES ONE AT A
TIME.

    Shape A (short_sha_for_row)  insertion brings its OWN doc
                                 -> stolen doc is 2+ added lines from the fn
    Shape B (candidate)          insertion has no doc
                                 -> stolen doc is immediately before the fn

I wrote a detector for each. EACH RETURNED A CONFIDENT EMPTY RESULT FOR THE
OTHER SHAPE, and I only noticed because I already knew both answers. Had I run
either one alone on an unknown commit I would have reported "no stranded
docs" and been wrong.

SO THE GATE SHOULD ASSERT ON THE RESULTING FILE, NOT ON THE DIFF. One
file-level invariant - every /// block is immediately followed by the item it
documents - covers both shapes and any future one. A diff-level detector has
to model every insertion shape and will be silently blind to the one nobody
thought of, which is this spec's own defect class reproduced inside its
remedy. Worth routing to BUG-1550's agent now rather than after they build it.

CONDITION RECORDED, not an objection: fix-only is right ONLY IF BUG-1550's
gate lands. One commit produced two instances in a single pass, so the rate is
not low, and if that spec stalls this class has no guard. Suggest a dependency
link rather than two independent specs.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2051 approved - all 3 checks confirmed; I approved the commit that caused it; and BUG-1550's gate must assert on the FILE not the diff (2 shapes, each detector blind to the other)
